caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 922 of 2003
lawyer:
Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate, instructed by S.R. Khoshnabish, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Chowdhury M. Zahangir Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No. 4 
Respondent Nos. 1-3 & 5-13 ------ Not represented.
parties:
Bijoy Kumar Sarbabidya ---- Petitioner
Vs.
Government of Judgment Bangladesh & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 6. As it appears the High Court Division found that no title deed being executed by the original owners or by any one on their behalf in favour of the plaintiff, no title passed to the plaintiff; though in paragraph 4 of the plaint the plaintiff made an averment about adverse possession but ended by asserting that he has acquired indefeasible right, title and interest in the suit property under section 53-A of the Transfer of the Property Act; none of the P.Ws. made any statement that the plaintiff had been possessing the suit land adversely against the original owners and no prayer was also made for declaration of title on the basis of adverse possession and the plaintiff in the plaint merely prayer for passing a decree declaring the title of the plaintiff in the suit land as its absolute owner though in order to make out a case of adverse possession it must be pleaded that adverse possession commenced and continued against the rightful owner but in the plant no such case of adverse possession was at all pleaded not to speak of proving such adverse possession; in the instant case there is also no evidence as to when the plaintiff started to possess adversely against real owners and when such possession became hostile; P.W.1 in her deposition admitted that even after the full payment no attempt was made to get any document from the original owners and no demand was also made for executants of any documents; the evidence on record shows that the plaintiff claimed to have entered into possession in the suit land on the basis of the agreement and as such the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land is permissive and if possession is found to be permissive at its inception the possessor cannot claim adversely to the grantor of the possession and the question of adverse possession does not arise where there has been no refusal on the part of the proposed vendor to execute the sale-deed and the possession of the vendee may be permissive even if the vendor has received the entire consideration money; the principle laid down in the cases of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), petitioner in C.R No. 372 of 1999 and Abdur Rashim vs. Md. Rezauddin Pk and others in reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76 on which the learned Advocate of the petitioner relied in support of his contention that exhibit-23 has a presumption of correctness, is not applicable in the instant case as the very execution of exhibit-23 having not been proved by sufficient and competent evidence the provisions of section 90 of the Evidence Act regarding presumption of genuineness of document which is 30 years old, has no manner of application in the instant case; the case of Md. Ashraf Ali and another-vs. Fatiq Chandra Saha and others reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 315 and the case of Santipada Datta & others-vs. Satish Chandra Das and others reported in 54 DLR(AD) 173 relied on by the learned advocate for the petitioner to substantiate his contention that the plaintiff can maintain the suit for declaration of his title on the basis of adverse possession, is not also applicable in the instant case since no case of adverse possession has been made out in the plaint in that regard and in the plaint no prayer was sought for declaration of title on the basis of adverse possession and further the trial court did not decree the suit on the basis of adverse possession but under section 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act though the provisions of section 53-A does not create any title in the property but only protects the right of the transferee in part performance of contract; the plaintiff though adduced certain evidence of possession but could not prove any paper in support of payment of rent to the municipality immediately after the agreement though in the plaint it was stated that the title deeds and khatians were handed over by the original owners to the plaintiff at the time of execution of the agreement of sale and delivery of possession but no such document or khatian of the original owner have been proved in this case and the papers produced have no nexus with the delivery of possession on 30.8.1947; the plaintiff also failed to make out a case of their very entry in the suit land; the contents of exhibit-A show that the added respondents are the lessees under the government; further in the plaint the area of suit land was originally shown as 6 acres but subsequently by amendments one after another the area was ultimately reduced to only .79 acres; moreover the description of the suit being vague and indefinite no decree could be passed in the absence of any local investigation; the suit as framed is not maintainable as neither exhibit-1 nor exhibit-23 have been proved by sufficient evidence.
